chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan, who said, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

One of them asked me about a man who spent a night from the nights of Mina in Mecca, so I said, 'I do not know.' Then I asked him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about it?' He said, 'Upon him is the blood-offering (dam) if he spent the night.' I said, 'If what detained him was the matter he was engaged in from his tawaf and sa'i, and it was not for sleep or pleasure, is the same ruling upon him as upon this [man who stayed for other reasons]?' He said, 'This is not in the same position as that, and I love that the dawn breaks for him only while he is in Mina.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood-offering (a specific sacrificial animal offered as expiation)
key_terms.سَعْيِهِ: His walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of Tashriq

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who stays in Mecca instead of Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that spending the night in Mecca instead of Mina incurs a blood-offering (dam), emphasizing the importance of the Mina stay as a core pillar of Hajj. He distinguishes between delay caused by necessary ritual acts like tawaf and sa'i, which exempts one from the penalty, and delay for mere sleep or pleasure, which does not. The Imam’s preference for the pilgrim to remain in Mina until dawn reflects the scholarly view that the night stay is a distinct obligation rather than merely a transitional pause.
